{{Short description|British mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Charles Henry Sampson''' (1859-1936)<ref>{{cite news |title=CHARLES SAMPSON, EDUCATOR, 77, DEAD; Principal of Brasenose Was With That College at Oxford for More Than 50 Years. (Published 1936) |work=The New York Times |date=6 November 1936 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1936/11/06/archives/charles-sampson-educator-77-dead-principal-of-brasenose-was-with.html}}</ref> was [[List of Principals of Brasenose College, Oxford|Principal of Brasenose College, Oxford]], from 1920<ref>'University Intelligence' [[The Times]] Monday, July 26, 1920 Issue 42472p.9</ref>  until his death.<ref>[https://www.british-history.ac.uk/vch/oxon/vol3/pp207-219 British History On-line]</ref>

Sampson was born in [[Bristol]] and educated at [[Bristol Grammar School]] and [[Balliol College, Oxford]]. A [[mathematician]], he became a [[Fellow]] of Brasenose in 1882; a [[Tutor]] in 1884; and a [[Tutor|Senior Tutor]] in 1894.<ref>{{Who's Who | title=Sampson, Charles Henry| id = U158530  | type = was | volume = 1920–2016 | edition = April 2014 online | access-date = 20 May 2020 }}</ref>

His son Ronald died in the [[World War I|Great War]].<ref>[http://lib.militaryarchive.co.uk/library/Biographical/library/The-Lancing-Roll-of-Honour-1914-1919/files/assets/basic-html/page128.html Lancing Roll of Honour]</ref> Sampson himself died on 5 November 1936.<ref>'The Principal Of Brasenose' [[The Times]] Saturday, Nov. 7, 1936 Issue 47526 p.14</ref>
